notes: ACCESS: Tier (a) HTTP-first only - curl_cffi (impersonate=chrome) + bs4/lxml against the live SSR HTML for every page (site returns fully server-rendered category pages, no browser needed). robots.txt fetched first: generic 'User-agent: * ' with path-specific Disallow rules (cart/checkout/my-account/search/filter/sale-collection paths) - none of it names Claude/anthropic bots and none of the URLs I used matched a Disallow pattern, so tier (a) was unblocked throughout; tiers (b)/(c) were not needed. TREE: union of (1) the mega-menu links embedded in the SSR homepage HTML (extracted via bs4), (2) https://www.danubehome.com/ae/en/sitemap.xml -> category_sitemap_ae_en.xml (1537 URLs), and (3) each candidate page's own rendered nav/links. Every leaf recorded was individually fetched and its H1 + <link rel=canonical> checked to match the requested slug; several sitemap slugs (e.g. /furnishings/curtains/furnishing-curtains, /kitchen/kitchenware/storage, /furnishings/carpets-and-rugs/prayer-mats) canonicalized to a different live URL and were deduped down to the canonical target per the duplicate rule. Two sitemap-only stub pages under a legacy singular '/furnishing/floor-covering/carpets-rugs/...' path (luxury-underfoot, solid) were excluded as stale/orphaned duplicates of the live 'furnishings' (plural) tree, unreachable from any nav, both showing 0 results. QTY: exact 'N Results' text scraped from each rendered category page (regex on visible page text), evidence recorded per row; zero-result style-facet rug pages (Digital, Kids, Persian Silk, Sisal) and Bathroom Trolley were kept with qty=0 since the site explicitly rendered '0 Results' for a genuinely distinct, live category page. EXCLUDED (Textile): 'Curtain Accessories' (14 results) - inspected product links, contents are curtain rods/tiebacks/rails (hardware) plus a couple of mesh door screens, so the category as a whole falls under the hardware boundary (textile.md SS5) and was dropped, keeping only 'Readymade Curtains'. 'Kitchen Organising' (1503, kitchen-wide mixed landing page combining dish rack/tools/knives/food storage) dropped as a non-textile parent with no textile children. EXCLUDED (Storage): 'Dish Rack' (385) - primary function is dish drying, not storage/organization, not in storage.md's kitchen-storage list. 'Lunch Boxes' - personal food-carry container, not home storage. 'Kitchen Organising' (1503) - mixed grouping/landing page (Dish Rack + Tools & Gadgets + Knife & Cutting Board + Food Storage), not a genuine storage-only category; used its real storage child 'Food Storage Containers & Jars' instead. 'Tool Boxes & Storage' (DIY/hardware path, 254) and 'Safes' (DIY path) excluded as out-of-scope hardware/security items, not home organization. 'Bathroom Accessories' > Accessory Singles/Sets (soap dish/dispenser/tissue-dispenser style items, same family as /bath/accessories/*) excluded as bathroom fixtures/accessories, not storage. 'Cleaning Tools' > Waste Bin (158) and Cleaning Mops And Accessories excluded - trash disposal / cleaning tools, not organizational storage. 'Clothes Drying And Ironing Board' (47) excluded per storage.md SS11 (ironing boards explicitly excluded; drying racks not storage). Furniture-nav items (furniture/bedroom-storage incl. Bedside Tables/Chest of Drawers/Dressing & Mirrors, furniture/office-furniture/storage-cabinets, furniture/living-room-furniture/shoe-cabinets-racks, book-cases-cabinets, wall-shelves) excluded because the site places them explicitly under its Furniture navigation branch - Furniture.xlsx territory, not re-litigated here. LOW/MEDIUM: 'Clothes Hangers' and 'Bathroom Trolley' marked MEDIUM confidence - hangers are not explicitly listed in storage.md's examples but sit under the site's own 'Closet Storage Solutions' organization group (ambiguity-handling SS42 rule 1: website hierarchy is the strongest signal); Bathroom Trolley matches storage.md SS20's 'Bathroom Storage Carts' example directly but currently shows 0 live products. 'Spice Racks & Jars' marked MEDIUM (matches storage.md SS13 'Spice Organizers' but the site bundles it with 'Jars' generally).
